## freshness comes from git history

ID: `instruction-audit/freshness-comes-from-git-history`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`scripts/scan_doc_freshness_ecosystem.py` SHALL date each active repository's root instruction file (AGENTS.md, else legacy CLAUDE.md) and top-level `docs/*.md` by the last commit that touched it, and SHALL report the drift against the repository's last code commit, never a self-declared date header.

Implemented by:

- `scan_doc_freshness_ecosystem` — [scripts/scan_doc_freshness_ecosystem.py:1](../../scripts/scan_doc_freshness_ecosystem.py#L1)

## instruction quality findings are advisory

ID: `instruction-audit/instruction-quality-findings-are-advisory`

Status: **implemented and tested**

`scripts/audit_instruction_quality.py` SHALL report oversized, misplaced, duplicated and derivable content in the instruction files of one repository (`--repo-root`) or of every repository in the project graph (`--all`), as text or `--json`, and SHALL NOT rewrite any instruction file.

## the project graph comes from the settings

ID: `instruction-audit/the-project-graph-comes-from-the-settings`

Status: **implemented and tested**

Both audits SHALL read the project graph named by `PROJECT_GRAPH`, else `~/code2/aes-config/PROJECT_GRAPH.json`, unless a path is given on the command line; they SHALL NOT read a graph beside the script.

Implemented by:

- `audit_instruction_quality` — [scripts/audit_instruction_quality.py:1](../../scripts/audit_instruction_quality.py#L1)
- `scan_doc_freshness_ecosystem` — [scripts/scan_doc_freshness_ecosystem.py:1](../../scripts/scan_doc_freshness_ecosystem.py#L1)

- Scenario `the-project-graph-comes-from-the-settings`: tested by `tests/test_scan_doc_freshness_ecosystem.py::test_the_project_graph_comes_from_the_settings` ([tests/test_scan_doc_freshness_ecosystem.py:75](../../tests/test_scan_doc_freshness_ecosystem.py#L75))
